headline: Two scientists say two papers in an Elsevier journal were probably written by AI and falsely claim to analyse public brain-scan data.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a clear integrity case, but the allegations are unproven and involve two papers.
summary: Retraction Watch, republished by The Scientist, reports that Dorothy Bishop, emeritus professor at the University of Oxford, and Kathy Rastle, a psychologist at the University of London, believe two 2026 papers in the Journal of Neurolinguistics were generated by AI and did not truly analyse the open brain-scan datasets they cite, one of which Rastle's team created. Elsevier, the journal's publisher, says it is investigating, while the author, Afzal Khan, says he is engaging with the journal and a correction is being processed.
importance_line: Researchers who share open data and journal readers are affected, but these are two scientists' allegations, nothing has been retracted, and the author says a correction is coming.
notes: The article says it was first published at Retraction Watch; Retraction Watch is credited as the first reporter.
